from.place: Assertion (3): compare the inverse-limit complex of a K-injective tower with the Roos cone

title: Roos complex computes inverse limit on K-injective towers
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with exact countable products and enough injectives, and let $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ be the abelian category of inverse systems [def-weil-inverse-system] in $\mathcal A$. Let $I_\bullet$ be a K-injective cochain complex of $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$, i.e. every morphism of complexes from an acyclic complex of $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ to $I_\bullet$ is homotopic to zero (the notion of [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions], with $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ in place of the category of sheaves). Write $P=\prod_n\operatorname{ev}_n(I_\bullet)$ for the termwise product complex, $P^p=\prod_n(I_n)^p$, and let $1-s:P\to P$ be the chain map given in each degree by the transition endomorphism of the inverse system $((I_n)^p)_n$ [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism]. Let $L^p=\varprojlim_n(I_n)^p$ be the termwise inverse limit, realized as $\ker(1-s:P^p\to P^p)$, with inclusion $\iota:L\to P$, and let $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ be the shifted mapping cone of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with terms $P^{p-1}\oplus P^p$ and differential $(y,x)\mapsto(-d_Py-(1-s)x,\,d_Px)$. Then the canonical map $\eta:L\to\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$, $\eta^p=(0,\iota^p)$, is a morphism of complexes and a quasi-isomorphism. Consequently $L$ and $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ represent the same object of $D(\mathcal A)$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 070M (lemma-difficulty-K-injectives), using Tag 0BK6 (lemma-product-K-injective); the arbitrary-tower form is obtained by replacing a K-injective representative by a termwise injective one

proof.text: Set-up. By [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ is abelian with kernels, cokernels, monomorphisms, epimorphisms and short exact sequences computed levelwise. For an inverse system $T=(T_n,f_n)$ in $\mathcal A$ let $P_T=\prod_nT_n$ (it exists: $\mathcal A$ has countable products) and $1-s_T$ its transition endomorphism [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism]. A morphism $x:Y\to P_T$ satisfies $(1-s_T)x=0$ iff its components $x_n=\mathrm{pr}_nx$ satisfy $x_n=f_n x_{n+1}$ for all $n$, i.e. iff $(x_n)$ is a cone over $T$ [def-weil-inverse-system]; hence $L_T:=\ker(1-s_T)$ with the maps $\mathrm{pr}_n\iota$ is $\varprojlim_nT_n$. By the naturality clause of [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism], $T\mapsto P_T$, $T\mapsto L_T$ are additive functors $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal A$ and $1-s$, $\iota$ are natural. Applied termwise to a complex $X$ of $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ they give complexes $P(X)=\prod_n\operatorname{ev}_n(X)$, $L(X)$ and chain maps $1-s:P(X)\to P(X)$, $\iota:L(X)\to P(X)$, and we put $\Phi(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ with the terms and differential of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] written in the statement. The map $\eta_X^p=(0,\iota^p)$ is a chain map: $d\eta(k)=(-(1-s)\iota k,\,d_P\iota k)=(0,\iota d_Lk)=\eta(dk)$ since $(1-s)\iota=0$. A chain map $\varphi:X\to X'$ induces $L(\varphi)$ and $\Phi(\varphi)=P(\varphi)^{p-1}\oplus P(\varphi)^p$, which is a chain map because $P(\varphi)$ commutes with $1-s$, and $\eta_{X'}L(\varphi)=\Phi(\varphi)\eta_X$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 070M (lemma-difficulty-K-injectives), proof: the first map of 0 -> I^p -> prod I_n^p -> prod I_n^p -> 0 'given by the projection maps' and the second by (x_n) -> (x_n - f_{n+1}(x_{n+1}))

proof.text: Homotopy invariance. Let $\varphi,\psi:X\to X'$ be chain maps of complexes of $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ with $\varphi-\psi=d h+h d$ for $h^p:X^p\to X'^{p-1}$. Since $L$ and $P$ are additive functors applied termwise, $L(\varphi)-L(\psi)=dL(h)+L(h)d$ and likewise for $P$; and $P(h)$ commutes with $1-s$ (naturality of $1-s$ in [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism]). On $\Phi$ put $H(y,x)=(-P(h)y,\,P(h)x)$; then $(DH+HD)(y,x)=\big((dP(h)+P(h)d)y-(1-s)P(h)x+P(h)(1-s)x,\ (dP(h)+P(h)d)x\big)=(\Phi(\varphi)-\Phi(\psi))(y,x)$, $D$ the differential of $\Phi$. So $L$ and $\Phi$ induce functors $K(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A))\to K(\mathcal A)$ on homotopy categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and $\eta$ is natural on them by Step 1.

source.place: Lemma Tag 070M, proof ('a corresponding distinguished triangle in K(A)'); the homotopy formula is written by the agent

proof.text: Split towers. Let $X=(X_n,g_n)$ be a split inverse system, with $g_n\sigma_n=\mathrm{id}$ (the notion of [lem-weil-tower-split-envelope]). Define $u:P_X\to P_X$ by $\mathrm{pr}_1u=0$ and $\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}u=\sigma_n(\mathrm{pr}_nu-\mathrm{pr}_n)$ (recursively, then by the universal property of the product). Then $\mathrm{pr}_n(1-s)u=\mathrm{pr}_nu-g_n\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}u=\mathrm{pr}_nu-g_n\sigma_n(\mathrm{pr}_nu-\mathrm{pr}_n)=\mathrm{pr}_n$, so $(1-s)u=\mathrm{id}$ and $1-s_X$ is a (split) epimorphism; with Step 1, $0\to L_X\xrightarrow{\iota}P_X\xrightarrow{1-s}P_X\to0$ is exact. This is the split short exact sequence $0\to I^p\to\prod I_n^p\to\prod I_n^p\to0$ of the source, there obtained from $I_{n+1}^p=C_{n+1}^p\oplus I_n^p$. A finite direct sum of split systems is split (take the direct sum of the sections).

source.place: Lemma Tag 070M, proof: 'We claim there is a split short exact sequence 0 -> I^p -> prod I_n^p -> prod I_n^p -> 0 ... The splitting comes from the map prod I_n^p -> prod C_n^p = I^p'

proof.text: The case of split terms. Let $J$ be a complex of $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ every term $J^p$ of which is a split inverse system. By Step 3 the chain map $1-s:P(J)\to P(J)$ is an epimorphism in every degree, with termwise kernel $\iota:L(J)\to P(J)$. By [lem-weil-degreewise-epi-kernel-cocone-qis], applied in $\mathcal A$ to $f=1-s$, the map $\kappa=(0,\iota)=\eta_J:L(J)\to\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]=\Phi(J)$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma Tag 070M, proof: 'We obtain a termwise split short exact sequence of complexes 0 -> I -> prod I_n -> prod I_n -> 0. Hence a corresponding distinguished triangle in K(A) and D(A)'

proof.text: Replacement by split terms. Apply the functor $E$ and the natural monomorphism $j:T\to E(T)$ of [lem-weil-tower-split-envelope] termwise to the complex $I_\bullet$: by naturality and additivity, $E(I_\bullet)$ is a complex and $j:I_\bullet\to E(I_\bullet)$ a chain map, monomorphic in each degree by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]; let $q:E(I_\bullet)\to C(I_\bullet)$ be its termwise cokernel, a chain map with the induced differential, so that $0\to I_\bullet\xrightarrow{j}E(I_\bullet)\xrightarrow{q}C(I_\bullet)\to0$ is short exact in each degree and $q$ is a degreewise epimorphism with kernel $j$. The terms of $E(I_\bullet)$ and of $C(I_\bullet)$ are split [lem-weil-tower-split-envelope]. Applying [lem-weil-degreewise-epi-kernel-cocone-qis] in the abelian category $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ to $q$ gives a quasi-isomorphism $u=(0,j):I_\bullet\to J:=\operatorname{Cone}(q)[-1]$, and $J^p=C(I_\bullet)^{p-1}\oplus E(I_\bullet)^p$ is split by Step 3.

source.place: Lemma Tag 070M; the replacement of the K-injective complex by a complex with split terms is written by the agent (the source works with the special inverse system of Lemma 13.29.3 / lemma-special-inverse-system, whose terms are split by construction)

proof.text: A homotopy retraction. $u$ is a quasi-isomorphism, so $Q(u)$ is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. As $I_\bullet$ is K-injective, $Q:\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(N,I_\bullet)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D}(QN,QI_\bullet)$ is bijective for every complex $N$ of $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Taking $N=J$ gives a chain map $r:J\to I_\bullet$ with $Q(r)=Q(u)^{-1}$; then $Q(ru)=\mathrm{id}=Q(\mathrm{id}_{I})$, and injectivity for $N=I_\bullet$ gives $ru\simeq\mathrm{id}_{I_\bullet}$ (chain homotopic).

source.place: agent-written; uses that maps into a K-injective complex are computed in K(A) (Lemma Tag 05TG, lemma-K-injective-defined, in the form of lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived)

proof.text: Conclusion. By Step 2, in $K(\mathcal A)$: $L(r)L(u)=L(ru)=\mathrm{id}$, $\Phi(r)\Phi(u)=\mathrm{id}$, $\eta_JL(u)=\Phi(u)\eta_I$ and $\eta_IL(r)=\Phi(r)\eta_J$. Apply $H^p$, which is defined on $K(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $v=H^p(L(r))\,H^p(\eta_J)^{-1}\,H^p(\Phi(u))$, using Step 4. Then $H^p(\eta_I)v=H^p(\Phi(r))H^p(\eta_J)H^p(\eta_J)^{-1}H^p(\Phi(u))=H^p(\Phi(ru))=\mathrm{id}$ and $vH^p(\eta_I)=H^p(L(r))H^p(\eta_J)^{-1}H^p(\eta_J)H^p(L(u))=H^p(L(ru))=\mathrm{id}$. So $H^p(\eta_I)$ is an isomorphism for every $p$: $\eta=\eta_{I_\bullet}:L\to\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and $Q(\eta)$ is an isomorphism $L\cong\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ in $D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

split_report.summary: Read Stacks derived.tex 070M (lemma-difficulty-K-injectives) with its proof and 0BK6 (lemma-product-K-injective). 070M proves the comparison only for the special system of lemma-special-inverse-system, whose terms satisfy I_{n+1}^p = C_{n+1}^p ⊕ I_n^p, so that 1-s is termwise split epi. The item is for an arbitrary K-injective complex of towers, so the split was written: Steps 1-3 set up lim, prod, 1-s, the cone and the map eta, prove homotopy invariance and that 1-s is split epi on split towers (elementary); Step 4 gets the split-term case from the new node lem-weil-degreewise-epi-kernel-cocone-qis; Step 5 replaces I by a quasi-isomorphic complex with split terms through the new node lem-weil-tower-split-envelope (Tow(A) levelwise by the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian); Step 6 uses K-injectivity through lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived to get a homotopy retraction r of u; Step 7 is the retract argument. Statement clarified (not changed in content): K-injective defined for Tow(A) explicitly (the cited definition node is for etale sheaves), L realized as ker(1-s), the cone and the map eta=(0,iota) written out. The hypotheses 'exact countable products' and 'enough injectives' are not used by the proof (only the existence of countable products); they are kept since the citer works in that setting.
